solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Siberian river with length and shape (6)

blocks.note: the Ob flows north across Siberia to the Arctic

annotation.surface: A geography note describing a Siberian river's length and outline.
annotation.walkthrough: The Ob is a crossword staple among rivers. The surface asks you to picture a river's course, but the last word, 'shape', is the definition on its own.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain category-and-member pairing: the oblong, a rectangle longer than it is wide, is one named shape.

entries.clue: Skater out in West Indies to practise another sport? (5,3)

indicators.note: 'out' as in out of order or out of joint: the skater's letters are no longer in their proper places
'in' puts the rearranged letters inside the West Indies, as a traveller is in the Caribbean

annotation.surface: An ice skater heads to the Caribbean to try something different.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is playful: a skater taking to the water in the Caribbean really would be switching sport.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic hint, not a synonym: water-skiing is a sport other than skating, so the skater's switch is the definition's joke.

entries.clue: Husband joining unruly originals blended language (5-5)

indicators.note: unruly children will not stay in line, and neither will these letters
'joining' has the husband attach himself to the group, so H is tacked on at the end

annotation.surface: A husband joins a band of unruly founding members, and their speech mixes together.
annotation.walkthrough: Husband comes first in the clue but its H goes last, after the rearranged letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose description rather than a synonym: Anglo-Irish mixes two national traditions, and 'blended' names that mixture.

entries.clue: Watch pressure slowly escape (4)

annotation.surface: An instruction to monitor a gauge as pressure bleeds away.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Watch' looks like a noun (a timepiece) but works as the verb see.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: liquid that oozes out through a crack little by little is getting away gradually.

entries.clue: Initial written cryptically around chimney enlightened people (10)

indicators.note: writing something in code scrambles it, so the initial's letters come out jumbled
'around' has the jumbled letters stand round the chimney, enclosing it

blocks.note: a lum is a chimney in Scots and northern English

annotation.surface: A coded initial scrawled around a chimney, a secret sign for a society in the know.
annotation.walkthrough: LUM is the Scottish word for a chimney, a regular crossword word. It sits after the first two letters of the rearranged INITIAL.
annotation.definitionFit: A literal translation: Latin illuminati means the ones lit up, and enlightened says the same in English.

entries.clue: Distinguished singer keen to make comeback (4)

indicators.note: a comeback is a return journey, so the word travels back the way it came, right to left

annotation.surface: A celebrated singer eager to return to the stage.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is the familiar story of a retired star's comeback, which is exactly what the letters of AVID do.
annotation.definitionFit: The Italian word diva means goddess, and it came to name a celebrated leading lady of opera.

entries.clue: Horned beast the thing with one foot raised (6)

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising the letters lifts the last to the top, so they read bottom to top

blocks.note: an animal's foot is a paw

annotation.surface: A horned animal standing with one hoof lifted.
annotation.walkthrough: The picture of a beast with a paw raised fits the wordplay neatly: in the grid the whole string ITIPAW is raised.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose description: the wapiti is a large North American deer, and its antlers are called horns in everyday speech.

entries.clue: Company receives order beginning to march with soldier (8)

indicators.note: a company that receives visitors takes them in, so CO holds the other pieces inside
the beginning of march is its first letter

annotation.surface: A military company gets its marching orders and is joined by a soldier.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a command to march, but it is OM, the Order of Merit. 'With' is also wordplay (AND), not a joining word.
annotation.definitionFit: A general-to-specific definition: a commando is one kind of soldier, trained for raids behind enemy lines.

entries.clue: Female supporter incarcerated shows little intellectual capacity (5,4)

annotation.surface: A woman who backed a cause is locked up and shows she is not very bright.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Female supporter' suggests a woman who backs someone; it is the undergarment.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: saying someone has only one brain cell is a joking jibe that they are not bright.

entries.clue: Maybe comma adds nothing to one publication (5)

annotation.surface: An editor's gripe that a comma contributes nothing to a piece of writing.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma here is not punctuation but a butterfly, named for the comma-shaped mark on its wing; 'maybe' signals that it is just one example.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the adult winged stage of an insect is its imago, and a comma butterfly is one such adult.

entries.clue: Share common ground having finished circuit (7)

blocks.note: a lap is one circuit of a track

annotation.surface: Runners who have completed a lap end up on the same stretch of ground.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition comes first and the wordplay pieces arrive in the order the answer reads them.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative phrase for the verb: two areas that partly cover each other have ground in common.

entries.clue: Posh princess uses mains leads for element (7)

indicators.note: whatever leads comes at the front, so each word gives its first letter

blocks.note: a rani is an Indian princess
first letters of uses and mains

annotation.surface: A posh princess plugs into the mains to power a heating element.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is about electrical mains leads and a heating element; 'leads' actually means first letters, and 'element' is a chemical one.
annotation.definitionFit: A category-and-member pairing: uranium, the radioactive metal, is one of the chemical elements.

entries.clue: Theatre Cat in squall losing tail (3)

indicators.note: a word's tail is its last letter, and here it is lost

blocks.note: GUST, a squall, without its last letter

annotation.surface: A theatre cat caught in a gust of wind and losing its tail.
annotation.walkthrough: Gus the Theatre Cat is from T. S. Eliot's Old Possum's Book of Practical Cats, the source of the musical Cats.
annotation.definitionFit: A named character: Eliot's poem Gus: The Theatre Cat gives him that very title.

entries.clue: See 21
Outline location accommodating upper-class in sprawling hotel (10)

indicators.note: a place that accommodates guests houses them, so SITE holds the rest inside
'in' puts the upper-class letter inside the hotel
a sprawling building spreads untidily, and so do the hotel's letters

annotation.surface: A description of a rambling hotel with a posh wing on the site.
annotation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: U goes into the rearranged HOTEL, and that whole run goes inside SITE after its first two letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: a silhouette is a shape shown only by its dark edge, which is what an outline is.

entries.clue: Certain changes in Danube and Nile (10)

indicators.note: changes made in the rivers' names alter the order of their letters

annotation.surface: A remark that there are certain changes happening along two great rivers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Certain' looks like it means 'some' changes; it is the definition, meaning sure.
annotation.definitionFit: An adjective synonym: what cannot be denied is beyond doubt, the sense of certain here.

entries.clue: Do cut off a sexual urge, providing excuse (5)

indicators.note: something cut off is severed from the end, so DO is chopped from the tail

blocks.note: the letters removed from the end

annotation.surface: Someone claims that curbing their desires gives them a handy excuse.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like the verb, but it is the letters DO, cut from the end of A LIBIDO.
annotation.definitionFit: A noun synonym: an alibi began as a claim to have been elsewhere and widened to any excuse.

entries.clue: Fool with heraldic device not quite put together (8)

indicators.note: a word that is not quite there stops just short of its end

annotation.surface: A fool whose coat of arms is only half finished.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' could apply to 'put together', but it trims the emblem to EMBLE.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb synonym, as when flat-pack furniture is fitted into one piece.

entries.clue: Land that’s green and somewhat pleasant (3)

indicators.note: 'somewhat' means to some extent, so only a part of the next word is taken

annotation.surface: An echo of Blake's 'England's green and pleasant land'.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue borrows the line 'England's green and pleasant land' from Blake's hymn Jerusalem, so the definition hides in a quotation.
annotation.definitionFit: A poetic word for a meadow, grassland that is green by nature.

entries.clue: Two passes for Maradona? (5)

blocks.note: a pass in a game is a go, a turn

annotation.surface: A football question about a pair of passes played to Maradona.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all football, but neither pass is kicked: one is to pass away, the other is a turn. Diego Maradona was the Argentine football star.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Maradona is one famous Diego, the question mark showing he stands for the first name.

entries.clue: Somehow at peace crossing southern region in NZ (4,4)

indicators.note: done somehow means done in some unspecified way, so the letters take some new order
the rearranged letters lie across the S, one part either side of it

annotation.surface: A traveller somehow finds peace crossing the south of New Zealand.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface points south, but East Cape is at the eastern tip of New Zealand's North Island.
annotation.definitionFit: A named place: East Cape is the headland and district at the eastern tip of New Zealand's North Island.

entries.clue: Forger in situ, no saint, into working for museums group (11,11)

indicators.note: letters set working are put to use in a new arrangement, as clay is worked into a shape

blocks.clueFragment: in situ, no saint, into working
blocks.note: IN SITU NO SAINT INTO rearranged

annotation.surface: A forger caught at the scene, no saint, getting into work for a museum group.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Forger' suggests a counterfeiter, which suits museums, but it is an honest blacksmith. The answer runs on into 14 across.
annotation.definitionFit: A named institution: the Smithsonian runs a family of national museums in Washington, DC.

entries.clue: I want to cuddle daughter? Absolutely (6)

indicators.note: to cuddle someone is to wrap your arms round them, so I NEED wraps round D

annotation.surface: A parent asks whether they want a hug from their daughter, and answers yes.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a question and its reply; the reply is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An interjection synonym: both are emphatic ways of saying yes.

entries.clue: Everything or unspecified amount for an audience? (3)

indicators.note: an audience hears rather than reads, so the word is taken by its sound

annotation.walkthrough: The two halves pull against each other, everything against some, yet they share a sound.
annotation.definitionFit: A noun synonym: the sum is the total, the whole amount taken together.

entries.clue: Old woman on edge about year in chaotic state (6)

indicators.note: in a down clue, whatever sits on something is placed above it
'about' means round, so the pair goes round the year

blocks.note: a hem is an edge of cloth

annotation.surface: An old woman on edge about a year spent in chaos.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On edge' reads as nervous, but here it just places one piece above another.
annotation.definitionFit: A noun synonym: mayhem, once a legal word for maiming, now means violent disorder.

entries.clue: Give drugs to banish cold and help settle (7)

indicators.note: to banish is to send into exile, so the C is sent out of the word

annotation.surface: A doctor's advice: dose to cure a cold and help the patient rest.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a medical cure for a cold; the definition is about disputes.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb synonym: a go-between who mediates helps the two sides reach agreement.

entries.clue: Continuous pain? One should ring hospital (4)

indicators.note: a ring encircles, so the one goes round the hospital

blocks.note: an ace is a one in cards

annotation.surface: Someone in constant pain is urged to phone the hospital.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like phoning; it means surround.
annotation.definitionFit: A noun synonym: an ache is a dull pain that goes on, as against a sharp stab.

entries.clue: Complete disorder with an unknown spanner thrown in? (7)

indicators.note: something thrown in lands inside, as a spanner is thrown in the works

annotation.surface: Throwing a spanner in the works leads to complete chaos.
annotation.walkthrough: The spanner is not the tool thrown into the works but an arch, which spans.
annotation.definitionFit: A noun synonym: from Greek 'without a ruler', anarchy is lawless disorder.

entries.clue: Giving away copyright lightens up relief (4)

indicators.note: whatever you give away you no longer have, so the word parts with its C

blocks.note: C = copyright, as in the © symbol; removed

annotation.surface: Giving up copyright eases the mind and brings relief.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Giving away' fits the charity of the answer but here means removing C from CALMS.
annotation.definitionFit: An older sense of relief: help for the poor, which is what alms are.

entries.clue: Slippery character back needing check calls for doctor (5)

indicators.note: sending a word back returns it the way it came, so EEL reads right to left

annotation.surface: A slippery type with a bad back who needs a check-up calls the doctor.
annotation.walkthrough: Leech is an old word for a doctor, from when physicians bled patients with leeches.
annotation.definitionFit: An archaic sense: leech was the Old English word for a physician.

entries.clue: Ample set rebuilt to accommodate one photography option? (4-5)

indicators.note: a rebuilt set is put together anew, so its letters take a new order
to accommodate a guest is to house them, so the I goes inside

annotation.surface: A roomy film set is rebuilt to fit in one more camera setup.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Set' suggests a film set; here it is just letters to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: shooting frames at long intervals is one technique a photographer may choose.
